content.question_text: In general terms, what does null handling mean in the context of switch pattern matching?

core_requirements: Switches can explicitly handle a null selector value using a case null, instead of throwing a NullPointerException like a classic switch would.
acceptable_variations: You can add a case for null so the switch doesn't crash when the value is null.

content.question_text: In general terms, what is a guard in a switch pattern?

core_requirements: A guard is an extra condition attached to a case (using the when keyword) that must also be true for that case to be selected.
acceptable_variations: An additional if-like condition added to a case.

content.question_text: In general terms, what does it mean for a switch to be exhaustive?

core_requirements: Every possible value the switch could receive must be covered by some case, so the switch always has somewhere to go.
acceptable_variations: All possible cases are accounted for, nothing is left unhandled.

content.question_text: In general terms, what is dominance in a switch with pattern cases?

core_requirements: Dominance is when an earlier, broader case makes a later case impossible to ever reach, which causes a compile-time error.
acceptable_variations: An earlier case 'blocks' a later one from ever matching.

content.question_text: In general terms, what restriction exists around using constants (like numbers or specific strings) inside record patterns?

core_requirements: You cannot directly match against a constant value inside a record pattern — you have to use a guard condition instead to check the value.
acceptable_variations: Record patterns can't check for exact constant values directly; a guard is needed instead.

content.question_text: In general terms, what is the variable scope/fallthrough issue that can occur with pattern variables in a switch?

core_requirements: A variable introduced by a pattern is only usable in that case (and if execution falls through, in limited situations) — trying to use it after falling into a different, unrelated case can cause errors.
acceptable_variations: Pattern variables have tricky scoping rules around fallthrough between cases.
